short: Optical-flow tower (M05) and mel-to-linear post-net (M06) are standard: no flow gain in Table 5; trails Le Cornu on S3; no listener test (M12); Lip2Wav's re-run: 27.83% vs 14.08% WER.
position: The paper [@ephrat2017improved] changes the visual input (M05: an optical-flow tower beside full-face pixels) and the decoder (M06: a mel-to-linear post-net, then Griffin-Lim); both are standard on its own evidence. Flow lowers STOI from 0.670 to 0.665 on GRID S3 in one reported split (Table 5); the full-model row adds 0.015, but it mixes two synthesis paths (M06). The gain over Vid2speech [@ephrat2017vid2speech] holds on objective scores (S4 STOI 0.584 to 0.700, Table 3), but on S3 Le Cornu and Milner [@lecornu2017generating] [concurrent] score higher ESTOI (0.437 against 0.398) and PESQ (2.055 against 1.974) in the same table. The evaluation (M12) drops the listener test both comparators ran; in Lip2Wav's [later] re-run of this method in its own setup it scores 27.83% WER on GRID and 53.52% on TCD-TIMIT, against 14.08% and 31.26% for Lip2Wav [@prajwal2020learning]. The "unconstrained dictionary" result rests on one of three TCD-TIMIT speakers (Table 4).
